messages:
Maya: Night handoff — ongoing incident affecting hosted and dedicated inference. I'm primary until 8pm PT. Quick summary below and actions for next shift.

Sam: Noted. Customer-facing 5xx spike started ~40m ago. Alerts tripped for /v1/generate and embeddings queue backlog in eu-west-1.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-API-THRASH created by alertmanager. Severity: P2. Pagers: Maya, Sam.

Jordan: What we see: dedicated-pool-3 is oscillating (scale thrash), which is producing higher queue latency and router timeouts. When pool evicts and respawns GPUs, KV cache warms causing extra latency.

Lia: Product note — we switched a few heavy customers to quantized fallback; some prompts show degraded output quality. Flagged to product but we should avoid long-term routing to quant variants.

Maya: Active alerts (current):
- high_error_rate:/v1/generate (5xx rate > 2% over 5m)
- queue_length:embeddings-eu (queue > 2500)
- gpu_sched:dedicated-pool-3 (scale events >3 in 15m)
- model_quality:quant-fallback-regression (sample fail rate elevated)

Maya: Mitigations in progress:
- Lowered autoscale aggressiveness on dedicated-pool-3 (temporary conservative policy).
- Enabled read-through cache on embeddings store in eu-west-1 to reduce upstream pressure.
- Limited routing to spare-pool-quant for a small canary set only.

Sam: Commands executed (for audit):
```
# make autoscale less aggressive
redwoodctl pools update dedicated-pool-3 --autoscale-policy conservative
# enable embeddings read-through per region
redwoodctl features set embeddings-readthrough --region eu-west-1 --on
# restrict routing to quant fallback to canary tag
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --fallback quant --tags canary-only
```

Sam: Quick logs showing router 504s and queue depth (excerpt):
```
2026-03-14T18:12:04Z router-1 GET /v1/generate 504 route=dedicated-pool-3 retries=2
2026-03-14T18:12:05Z router-1 POST /v1/embeddings 504 queue_depth=2701
2026-03-14T18:12:06Z scheduler-2 scale_event up->down pool=dedicated-pool-3 reason=preemption
```

Jordan: Short-term runbook pointers to hand off:
- Autoscale thrash runbook: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/autoscale-thrash
- Embeddings backlog & read-through: https://internal.redwood.com/runbooks/embeddings-backpressure
- Routing fallback docs (how to failover heavy customers): https://internal.redwood.com/ops/routing-fallback

Jordan: Escalation thresholds (what to watch for):
- If embeddings queue > 3000 for > 10m -> manual shard add `redwoodctl queues add-shard embeddings eu-west-1`
- If sustained 5xx > 5% for 15m -> trigger cross-region failover for top 10 customers (see routing doc)
- If scale thrash events > 6 in 30m -> page infra-sre immediately and consider cordoning pool

Lia: Coverage gap to note: APAC on-call rotation is offline until 03:00 PT. If latency spreads to ap-northeast or we need on-prem intervention, escalate to oncall-manager or use the paging matrix.

Maya: Ownership for next shift: Sam will be primary from 20:00 PT, Jordan secondary. Lia will own product-facing quality comms if we need to contact customers.

Sam: I accept handoff. Plan: monitor error rates, give status update every 30m, and run the manual shard add if queue > 3000. Will also coordinate with infra-sre if thrash resumes.

Maya: Extra notes for Sam: check `metrics.high_error_rate` dashboard and the `router-logs` live tail in Kibana query saved as "ongoing-inc-API-THRASH". If you need to revert route changes, use the rollback sequence in the routing doc.

Sam: Acknowledged. I'll run a sanity canary on a couple of affected customers before broad changes.

Maya: Handoff complete. Leaving channel open — will be reachable by DM for 15m. Good luck. :wave: :rotating_light:

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Incident INC-2026-API-THRASH assigned to Sam (primary) and Jordan (secondary). Reminder: update the incident timeline and tag evidence (`/inc timeline add`) if you take manual actions.
